claims.text: There are two main types of data: quantitative and qualitative.
claims.quote: We distinguish between two main types of data: quantitative and qualitative.

claims.text: Quantitative data are data that can be written as numbers.
claims.quote: Quantitative data are data that can be written as numbers.

claims.text: Quantitative data can be discrete or continuous.
claims.quote: Quantitative data can be discrete or continuous.

claims.text: Discrete quantitative data can be represented by integers and usually occur when we count things.
claims.quote: Discrete quantitative data can be represented by integers and usually occur when we count things

claims.text: Examples of discrete quantitative data given in the book are the number of learners in a class, the number of molecules in a chemical solution, and the number of SMS messages sent in one day.
claims.quote: for example, the number of learners in a class, the number of molecules in a chemical solution, or the number of SMS messages sent in one day

claims.text: Continuous quantitative data can be represented by real numbers.
claims.quote: Continuous quantitative data can be represented by real numbers

claims.text: Examples of continuous quantitative data given in the book are the height or mass of a person, the distance travelled by a car, and the duration of a phone call.
claims.quote: for example, the height or mass of a person, the distance travelled by a car, or the duration of a phone call

claims.text: To classify a data set as quantitative and discrete, check whether it is a count represented by integers: a count represented by an integer is quantitative and discrete (the number of SMS messages sent the previous day by each of 20 classmates is an example).
claims.quote: The number of SMS messages is a count represented by an integer, which means that it is quantitative and discrete.

claims.text: A table of counts, such as how many times each colour appears, is a discrete quantitative data set because each count is an integer.
claims.quote: This is a discrete quantitative data set since each count is an integer.

claims.text: Qualitative data are data that cannot be written as numbers.
claims.quote: Qualitative data are data that cannot be written as numbers.

claims.text: Two common types of qualitative data are categorical data and anecdotal data.
claims.quote: Two common types of qualitative data are categorical and anecdotal data.

claims.text: Categorical data can come from one of a limited number of possibilities.
claims.quote: Categorical data can come from one of a limited number of possibilities

claims.text: Examples of categorical data given in the book are your favourite cooldrink, the colour of your cell phone, and the language that you learnt to speak at home.
claims.quote: for example, your favourite cooldrink, the colour of your cell phone, or the language that you learnt to speak at home

claims.text: Anecdotal data take the form of an interview or a story.
claims.quote: Anecdotal data take the form of an interview or a story

claims.text: An example of anecdotal data given in the book is asking someone what their personal experience was when using a product.
claims.quote: when you ask someone what their personal experience was when using a product

claims.text: To classify a data set as categorical qualitative data, check whether each response comes from one of a small number of possibilities (for example, a small number of possible colours).
claims.quote: This is a categorical qualitative data set since each of the responses comes from one of a small number of possible colours.

claims.text: Categorical qualitative data are sometimes turned into quantitative data by counting the number of times that each category appears.
claims.quote: Categorical qualitative data are sometimes turned into quantitative data by counting the number of times that each category appears.

claims.text: The same data can be represented in a different way by counting how many times each category (for example, each colour) appears.
claims.quote: We can represent exactly the same data in a different way, by counting how many times each colour appears.

claims.text: To classify a data set as qualitative and categorical, check that each response is not a number but one of a small number of possibilities (for example, which cellular provider a learner uses).
claims.quote: Since each response is not a number, but one of a small number of possibilities, these are categorical qualitative data.
